what: French military built the Antoinette barrel, a ground trainer for aircraft pilots

sources.title: Flight simulator
sources.quote: In 1910, on the initiative of the French commanders Clolus and Laffont and Lieutenant Clavenad, the first ground training aircraft for military aircraft were built.

note: Earlier than first pass (Link 1929). Antoinette barrel was a crude manually moved mock-up with controls; fit to instruments/motion is loose, hence low. Link Trainer (1929) is the first instrumented, pneumatically moved device; no earlier fully fitting one found.

what: Antoinette barrel used for military ground training of pilots in France

sources.title: Flight simulator
sources.quote: In 1910, on the initiative of the French commanders Clolus and Laffont and Lieutenant Clavenad, the first ground training aircraft for military aircraft were built.

note: Same event as demonstration; the source says it was built for military training. Link Trainer's 1934 USAAF purchase is later, so rejected as earliest.

what: Link Trainers mass-produced and used to train most Allied pilots in WWII

sources.title: Flight simulator
sources.quote: Some 10,000 were produced to train 500,000 new pilots from allied nations

sources.title: Flight simulator
sources.quote: The best-known early flight simulation device was the Link Trainer, produced by Edwin Link in Binghamton, New York

note: Year is approximate (wartime training 1941-45). Training of ordinary recruits, not consumers; consumer sims came later (1980s) and are not earlier.

what: Ivan Sutherland and students built a computer-driven head-mounted display (Sword of Damocles) at Harvard

sources.title: The Sword of Damocles (virtual reality)
sources.quote: The system was created in 1968 by computer scientist Ivan Sutherland with the help of his students Bob Sproull

note: Heilig's Sensorama (1962) rejected: mechanical, not computer-generated. Philco Headsight (1961) is camera-based, not a generated world. Primitive wireframe, so fit is partial.

what: Virtuality 1000CS arcade VR machines released for public use

sources.title: Virtuality (product)
sources.quote: Virtuality produced an arcade variant of the 1000SU for public use called the 1000CS which was released in 1991.

note: Earlier military/NASA uses (e.g. flight simulators with helmet displays, 1980s) may exist but were not verified; low confidence.

what: MUD (MUD1) created by Roy Trubshaw and Richard Bartle at Essex University, a multi-user shared text world

sources.title: MUD1
sources.quote: MUD was created in 1977 by Roy Trubshaw and Richard Bartle at the University of Essex on a DEC PDP-10.

note: Earlier: Maze War (two networked computers, 1973) and PLATO games like Empire (1973) are multi-user but game arenas rather than a world to meet in; considered and rejected, though arguable. First pass chose Habitat 1986 (graphical), later than MUD.

what: MUD1 opened over the Internet to outside players, the first Internet multiplayer online RPG

sources.title: MUD1
sources.quote: That same year, MUD1 became the first Internet multiplayer online role-play

note: Public remote play grew from 1983; Habitat (1986 beta, Club Caribe 1988) is later.

what: World of Warcraft passed 10 million subscribers

sources.title: World of Warcraft
sources.quote: On January 22, 2008, World of Warcraft had more than 10 million subscribers worldwide

note: Year is a judgment; online worlds were popular from about 2004-2005, but routine use by ordinary people is arguable.
